definitions.explanation: The state of all available items or tickets having been sold, with none remaining. Used for merchandise, tickets, and limited-edition products.

examples.japanese: チケットは{完売|かんばい}した。
{限定|げんてい}{商品|しょうひん}は{発売|はつばい}{初日|しょにち}に{完売|かんばい}した。
examples.english: The limited-edition product sold out on the first day of release.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}のコンサートだったので、チケットは{発売|はつばい}{開始|かいし}{数分|すうふん}で{完売|かんばい}になった。
examples.english: Since it was a popular concert, tickets sold out within minutes of going on sale.

notes:
Composed of {完|かん} (complete) + {売|ばい} (sell). Indicates that all stock or tickets have been sold with none remaining.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {完売|かんばい}する: to sell out (active)
- {完売|かんばい}になる: to become sold out (change of state)
- {完売|かんばい}{済|ず}み: sold out (already completed)
- {完売|かんばい}{御礼|おんれい}: thank you, sold out (seen on signs)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チケットが{完売|かんばい}する: tickets sell out
- {即日|そくじつ}{完売|かんばい}: sold out the same day
- {発売|はつばい}{開始|かいし}{直後|ちょくご}に{完売|かんばい}: sold out immediately after going on sale

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {売|う}り{切|き}れ: sold out (more colloquial, used in everyday speech and shop signs)
- {品切|しなぎ}れ: out of stock (focuses on availability rather than sales)

REGISTER:
{完売|かんばい} is more formal than {売|う}り{切|き}れ and is commonly used in business, event, and media contexts.
